rows.description: A child who stumbles while reading makes a silly face and gets the class laughing with them; the joke keeps control of the moment, though constant clowning can hide worry.

A teenager uses ugh for irritation, fatigue or dramatic humour. Others may take it as rudeness, but often it is harmless venting; a teen can learn to add a few words such as that was a long day to avoid confusion.

rows.subtype: Feeling like a fraud in a top college [Actor]
rows.description: A student admitted to a prestigious institute believes they got in by luck and that everyone will soon find out; success is discounted while comparison with others is harsh.

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: The person asks a basic question and the reply is kind and matter-of-fact. The feared humiliation does not arrive, and the belief that ignorance must be hidden starts to loosen.
A child who stumbles while reading makes a silly face and gets the class laughing with them; the joke keeps control of the moment, though constant clowning can hide worry.

A student is drawn to a classmate's humour and confidence and imagines a future from a few conversations. Infatuation fills in the blanks generously, so the person seen is partly the person wished for.
A child says a project will be quick and starts the night before. He imagines the ideal path and forgets past delays.

rows.subtype: Approach: thinks a task will take only a few minutes [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy says he will finish his drawing in ten minutes before dinner. It takes an hour, and he ends up upset when his mother calls.
A teenager delays a project because a poor result would reveal weakness; putting it off protects the self-image but makes the eventual work worse.
Putting the task off gives an immediate lift, followed by a background hum of guilt. The relief rewards the avoiding, so the pattern strengthens each time it works.

rows.subtype: Restless and asking what to do [Actor]
rows.description: A child declares boredom after ten minutes and wants a screen; boredom is uncomfortable but can also be the doorway to imagination when adults give time and simple materials.
When I am bored I grab the phone and scroll. Boredom is where new ideas begin; sometimes I can try drawing, playing outside or reading instead.
